name: Nabil Zaghloul

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Zaghloul directs the Multnomah County social and economic program Bienestar de la Familia.
bio.excerpt: He’s currently the director of Multnomah County Social and Economic program Bienestar de la Familia

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Zaghloul has worked for Multnomah County for over 32 years, according to his campaign website.

collection_notes: 2024 Portland City Council District 2 coverage (OPB, WW, KATU, KOIN) was found but not used: it concerns a different race and is not 2026 material. Steps run identically for all 7 District 2 candidates. Voters' pamphlet: the SOS Book 13 and the county's regular and large-print Multnomah pamphlet PDFs are cut off by the fetch tool (~105-120k characters); the large-print text ends partway through Herman Greene's statement (p. 44), so pamphlet statements for Bri Williams, Serena Cruz, Nathan Ong Norris, Nabil Zaghloul and Tony Robertson (pp. 45-47) could not be read there. The county's Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide links an individual statement PDF for all 7 candidates; those for Cruz and Robertson are machine-readable, while those for Broussard, Greene, Williams, Ong Norris and Zaghloul are scans with no readable text (Broussard and part of Greene were read from the large-print pamphlet instead). SEL 101 candidate filings were machine-readable only for Cruz and Robertson (others scanned/empty). The Portland Mercury District 2 profile (2026-09-26) covers all 7 candidates and is the common T3 source. Step 5 ran with allowed_domains limited to opb.org, wweek.com, portlandmercury.com because the proxy rejected longer domain lists. Incumbency: the current District 2 commissioner is Shannon Singleton (multco.us/board), who is running for Chair, so no D2 candidate is the incumbent. The fetch tool limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some excerpts are fragments.
